Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Carry on where you left off**: the game keeps the player's place as it goes and when it quits, and the sample's title offers to carry on from it, with the scene and the date (`doc/kagex.txt`, "Carrying On and Quick Saves"). A script error in a release build saves it, and the read marks and settings, before the game ends
- **Quick saves that go round**: the last three quick saves are kept, so one wrong key can't overwrite the only one, and quick load asks, then loads the newest; Shift+S and Shift+L, and Q.SAVE and Q.LOAD on the sample's message window
- **Voices that fade out when cut**: clicking past a voiced line, or the next voice starting, fades the voice out over a moment instead of cutting it off mid-syllable, and the speaker's next voice starts at once; Config's new second page offers Stop, Fade or Keep and the fade's length
- **Voices from where the speakers stand**: a character on the left is heard from the left, one further back further away (`"voice3d" => true` in `envinit.tjs`; Config can centre them), and `[ai voice=12 vol=35]` makes one line a whisper, `pan=` puts it somewhere of its own (`doc/world.txt`, "Voice Specification"). The Character demo has a new Voices scene with Ai and Pip
- **The web build keeps its saves**: everything a web game saved used to go when the page was closed or reloaded; saves now stay in the browser
- kagex-release 0.16.0 downloads the 0.16.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.16.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
